title: YNH Plugin
description: Harness plugin manifest for ynh 0.2+ — lives at .ynh-plugin/plugin.json. Install-time provenance lives in a separate .ynh-plugin/installed.json file written by ynh install.

agent.description: Harness-level defaults for `ynh agent run`. Flags win over these; these win over the built-in defaults. Setting them here means a harness carries its own spend envelope rather than every caller passing flags.

max_wall.description: Wall-clock cap as a Go duration, e.g. "45m".

env_passthrough.description: Environment variables this harness may see. Governs two things deliberately: which ${VAR} references its MCP declarations may resolve, and which variables reach an agent worker's process. Absent or empty means none — a worker inheriting the operator's whole environment holds every credential the operator holds. A reference to a variable outside this list, or to one that is unset, is an error rather than an empty value.

profiles.description: Named configuration variants. Merge semantics: mcp_servers are deep-merged (profile keys win), hooks use per-event replace (profile event replaces default, absent events inherited), includes are appended to the base harness's includes when the profile is active. Set a server to null to remove it.

env_passthrough.description: Replaces the harness-level env_passthrough when this profile is selected. Replacement rather than union: a profile that exists to restrict what an agent can see has to be able to, and a union could only ever widen.

focuses.description: Named combinations of profile + prompt for repeatable AI execution.

sensors.description: Named observation surfaces declared by the harness. ynh declares; loop drivers run them. Each sensor is a role declaration over existing primitives — no new artifact type.

category.description: Fowler bucket — free metadata for loop-driver triage.

role.description: Optional role hint for loop drivers. regular = run between turns; convergence-verifier = the loop's done-check; stuck-recovery = invoked when the stuckness watchdog fires. Pure metadata — ynh does not enforce semantics. `convergence-verifier` requires a command or focus source: no verdict about a files sensor's contents is derivable, so a files sensor would end the run because a path exists and is newer than its inputs — with contents never read, and the path inside the agent's own write path, which the run could write itself.

tolerance.description: How `ynh check` treats a failing result. blocking (default) gates the run; advisory reports the failure without gating; report is pure observation. A command sensor gates on its exit code and a files sensor on its freshness; a focus sensor never gates, because resolving one needs an agent runtime ynh does not own.

version_command.description: Optional shell command that prints the version of the tool this sensor runs, e.g. "golangci-lint --version". Recorded on the result so a corpus graded across weeks can tell a genuine change in findings from the linter changing underneath it. Declared rather than inferred: guessing `<first token> --version` is wrong for a wrapper like `make lint`, and hangs on commands that do not support it. Failure to run it is never a sensor failure — the version is simply absent.

ratchet.description: How the baseline forgives this sensor's failures. `fingerprint` (default) matches individual findings, so a fixed one stops being forgiven and a new one is flagged wherever it appears. `count` ratchets the total instead, for a sensor whose quantity is the finding — suppression directives above all. Fingerprints normalise line numbers and deduplicate, so a second identical finding in a file that already has one is invisible to the default; `count` is what sees it. Requires a command source.

observes.description: For files sensors: the paths this sensor's artifact depends on, used to decide whether it still describes the tree. Omitted means the whole git-tracked tree, which is strict — any commit then marks the artifact stale. Patterns are not filepath.Glob: `**` descends to any depth, and a pattern resolving to a directory means that directory's whole subtree, so `services`, `services/*` and `services/**` observe the same files. Ignored for command and focus sensors, which observe by running.

sensor_source.description: Strict one-of: files | command | focus. The set field discriminates the sensor type.

format.description: Freeform format identifier — pass-through to loop driver. Conventional names: json, junit-xml, lcov-summary, sarif, markdown, text, ndjson.

channel.description: Where the result emerges. Conventional values: stdout, stdout+exit, file, files. Defaults are inferable from source.

profile_mcp_servers.description: MCP servers within a profile. Null removes an inherited server.

git.description: Remote Git URL or shorthand (e.g. github.com/org/repo). Mutually exclusive with local.

local.description: Local filesystem path. Absolute or relative to the harness root. Mutually exclusive with git.

ref.description: Git ref (branch, tag, SHA). Only meaningful when git is set.

path.description: Subdirectory within the resolved source. Must be relative and must not traverse above the source root.

pick.description: Artifact paths in canonical type/name form. Skills use the bare name (they are directories): skills/<name>. Flat artifacts include the .md extension: agents/<name>.md, rules/<name>.md, commands/<name>.md.

sensor_reference.description: A fixture with a known answer, run by `ynh check --calibrate` to prove the sensor still observes. Nothing else verifies that a sensor still detects what it claims to: a command that quietly stops examining anything exits 0 and the gate reports green.

path.description: Fixture directory, relative to the harness. Must live outside the agent's write path — a reference an agent can edit calibrates nothing.

expect.description: The result the fixture must produce. `fail` is the case that matters: a sensor that passes a fixture designed to trip it has stopped observing. `pass` catches the opposite failure, a sensor that fires on clean input.
